lead.headline: Asia-Pacific central banks and HSBC push regulated stablecoins into retail and cross-border rails while US regulators and lawmakers apply divergent pressure
lead.tldr: The stablecoin infrastructure race is splitting along regulatory fault lines: Asia-Pacific is building regulated, bank-issued channels while US authorities probe existing players and flag tokenization risks without creating clear on-ramps.

intro: Dear Founders, Investors, and Friends, today's brief tracks how the stablecoin stack is being built out by central banks and systemically important banks in Asia even as US oversight fragments between enforcement actions and examination priorities that stop short of rulemaking.

top_signals.title: Singapore, Malaysia and Thailand central banks expand cross-border stablecoin initiative involving Ripple, Visa and Mastercard
top_signals.summary: Central banks from Singapore, Malaysia, and Thailand are expanding the BLOOM initiative to enhance cross-border settlements. The project leverages regulated stablecoins and tokenized bank deposits in collaboration with major payment players like Ripple, Visa, and Mastercard.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The BLOOM expansion signals that ASEAN central banks are treating stablecoin infrastructure as a monetary policy tool rather than a crypto-native experiment, which reprices the strategic value of regulated issuance licenses in the region.

top_signals.title: HSBC launches Hong Kong dollar stablecoin for retail payments
top_signals.summary: HSBC has launched RedCoin, a Hong Kong dollar-pegged stablecoin designed for retail payments via the PayMe app. The bank intends to expand the utility of the token into institutional use and tokenized investments.
top_signals.why_it_matters: HSBC's retail stablecoin launch from a systemically important bank creates a template for how deposit-taking institutions can capture payment flows that would otherwise leak to unregulated issuers, with implications for every neobank and fintech stablecoin project in Asia.

top_signals.title: US senator probes Tether after reported deal with ex-Trump crypto adviser
top_signals.summary: The US Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations is probing Tether following reports of a deal with Nxum, a company co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines. The subcommittee has demanded records regarding the interactions between the two entities.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The Senate probe into Tether's reported Nxum dealings introduces political tail risk that extends beyond enforcement into potential legislative leverage, making USDC's regulatory positioning relatively more valuable for any treasury or payment use case requiring US market access.

top_signals.title: Initia halts network after security incident as attacker reportedly mints tokens
top_signals.summary: Initia has halted its network following a security incident involving the unauthorized minting of tokens. The breach was first reported by crypto researcher Spreek, though the total amount of tokens lost has not yet been confirmed.
top_signals.why_it_matters: Initia's halt after unauthorized minting is a reminder that appchain security assumptions break down at the bridge and minting-contract layer, which should factor into how we underwrite pre-mainnet or early-mainnet infrastructure valuations.

top_signals.title: SEC flags tokenization as high-risk area in 2027 market examinations48m, SEC flags tokenization as high-risk area in 2027 market examinationsThe SEC’s latest priorities highlight tokenization as an emerging market risk, while cryptocurrencies remain absent as a standalone examination category.
top_signals.summary: The SEC has identified tokenization as a high-risk area for its 2027 market examinations. Notably, while tokenization is flagged, cryptocurrencies are not listed as a standalone examination category in the latest priorities.
top_signals.why_it_matters: The SEC's tokenization flag without a standalone crypto category suggests examination risk will land on traditional finance intermediaries experimenting with on-chain products rather than native crypto protocols, potentially slowing institutional adoption timelines.

on_the_radar.title: China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildout4m, China targets 2030 for its national blockchain network buildoutChina’s five-year digital development plan calls for wider blockchain use in trade and manufacturing alongside stronger technical standards.
on_the_radar.summary: China has outlined a five-year digital development plan aiming to establish a national blockchain network by 2030. The initiative focuses on integrating blockchain into trade and manufacturing while establishing rigorous technical standards.

on_the_radar.title: New York AG seeks $1.37B from NovaTech founders over Ponzi scheme
on_the_radar.summary: The New York Attorney General is seeking $1.37 billion in restitution from the founders of NovaTech following allegations of operating a Ponzi scheme. Additionally, four promoters have already agreed to settlements totaling nearly $6 million.

on_the_radar.title: South Korea to amend forex law to regulate stablecoins as payment instruments: report
on_the_radar.summary: South Korea is planning to amend its foreign exchange laws to regulate stablecoins used as payment instruments. This move is part of the broader development of the Digital Asset Basic Act to create a comprehensive crypto framework.

on_the_radar.title: Bybit secures first full Dubai license for spot trading services
on_the_radar.summary: Bybit has obtained its first full spot trading license from Dubai's Virtual Assets Regulatory Authority (VARA). The exchange must fulfill further requirements before officially launching its services in the region.

on_the_radar.title: Wells Fargo and five others object to OKX-ICE tokenized stock listings: Report
on_the_radar.summary: Wells Fargo and five other companies, including Arm Holdings and Intuit, are objecting to the tokenized stock listings proposed by the OKX and ICE joint venture. This highlights ongoing friction between traditional corporate entities and the tokenization of equity on blockchain platforms.

on_the_radar.title: Netanyahu seeking blockchain plan to prepare for possible sanctions
on_the_radar.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is exploring the implementation of a blockchain-based plan to mitigate the impact of potential international sanctions. The strategy aims to leverage decentralized technology to maintain financial stability and trade capabilities.

on_the_radar.title: Bitcoin ETFs swing back to net outflows as $636 million in withdrawals erase previous day's inflows
on_the_radar.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs experienced significant net outflows of $635.6 million on Thursday. This movement effectively erased the gains from the previous day's $528.4 million in inflows.

on_the_radar.title: Ethereum delays Glamsterdam Hoodi testnet launch over security risks
on_the_radar.summary: Ethereum has postponed the launch of the Glamsterdam testnet fork following security warnings. The delay comes after ChainSecurity identified risks that proposed gas changes could compromise smart contract safeguards.

worth_a_read.note: Galaxy's analysis of Solana's Alpenglow upgrade focuses on whether technical improvements translate to sustained transaction growth, a necessary read for anyone underwriting Solana ecosystem exposure on throughput metrics alone.

worth_a_read.note: Messari's memecoin report examines whether speculative token mechanics are creating durable protocol revenue or merely redistributing retail capital, which matters for distinguishing casino liquidity from product-market fit in consumer crypto.

linkedin_post: The same week HSBC puts a Hong Kong dollar stablecoin in 2 million retail wallets via PayMe, three ASEAN central banks expand BLOOM with Ripple, Visa, and Mastercard. The stablecoin stack is being built by banks and monetary authorities, not by crypto startups. This is the repricing event. The US response: a Senate probe into Tether's reported ties to a former Trump adviser, and the SEC flagging tokenization as examination risk without creating a path to compliance. The divergence is now structural. Asia is issuing licenses and running pilots. The US is running investigations. For founders choosing jurisdictions, the cost of capital is shifting with it. We underwrite stablecoin infrastructure on where the regulatory surface area is shrinking, not where the headlines are loudest. The test: in twelve months, does a US bank launch a retail stablecoin, or does the first major cross-border ASEAN settlement clear on a regulated stablecoin rail? One of those happens. The other probably does not.
